events.content:
Tech companies are investing a lot of hope and money in rocks.

Google, Microsoft, and others have committed hundreds of millions of dollars to get startups to spread crushed basalt, olivine, or other alkaline materials across farms, in an effort to capture carbon from the air and lock it away. A number of influential models have found that this approach, known as enhanced rock weathering (ERW), could eventually remove 3 billion to 8 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide per year, helping to slow or one day even reverse global warming. An additional promise is that these applications of rock could help farmers by improving the quality of their soil.

But a pair of preprint studies set for release today raise serious questions about how much material could be added to that soil before it may actually reduce the crop yields that are essential to farmers’ livelihoods, MIT Technology Review can exclusively report. 

Cutting back on the rock applications to prevent these negative effects would shrink the method’s carbon dioxide removal capacity, likely capping it at less than a billion tons per year. The analyses were led by researchers at CarbonPlan, a San Francisco nonprofit known for rigorous scientific analysis of carbon removal methods.

These concerns come on top of a series of scientific questions about how to accurately estimate the carbon removal achieved through this approach and the possibility that some projects have overstated it, which researchers at CarbonPlan and elsewhere have raised in recent months and years.

“There’s still a heck of a lot we need to learn about ERW,” says Tyler Kukla, a research scientist at CarbonPlan and lead author of the new reports. “But a real tension, to me, exists between this massive amount of uncertainty and the big questions we have about whether or not this works, sitting alongside tremendous efforts to scale it up really quickly.” 

How it works

There is no scientific dispute that certain rocks and minerals help to sequester carbon. Rain captures carbon dioxide molecules as it falls through the atmosphere, forming carbonic acid. When it lands on exposed silicate materials, that weak acid dissolves or chemically “weathers” the rocks. 

The resulting calcium, magnesium, and carbon (in the form of bicarbonate) then travel on a long journey through creeks, streams, and rivers until they reach the ocean, where corals, mollusks, and other marine organisms may eventually use them to form calcium carbonate shells. As they die, those shells fall to the seafloor, combine with sediments, and form limestone rock that locks away the carbon.

If you thought that explanation was long, just imagine how long the process takes to unfold in real life! It’s not called the slow carbon cycle for nothing.

“Enhanced” rock weathering promises to accelerate the process. Grinding up the rocks and spreading them across fields creates much more surface area for carbonic acid to react with—and that should ultimately direct more carbon into the oceans.

ERW doesn’t require as much energy or infrastructure as other carbon dioxide removal options like direct-air-capture plants, and at least in the early rollout stages it can largely rely on waste material from rock mining operations.

But the big selling point is that there can be an economic benefit to doing it; it’s not just a cost like other forms of carbon removal. Added to agricultural soils, these sorts of rocks can increase nutrients, reduce acidity, and improve water retention, helping to boost crop yields (at least up to a point). Indeed, many farmers already routinely add crushed-up limestone to their soil to counteract the increased acidity caused by fertilizer use and other agricultural practices. 

So carrying out enhanced rock weathering could merely be a matter of switching to other types of rock with the potential to lock away more carbon (about twice as much as limestone).

events.title: 27 Cybersecurity Terms to Prepare You for the Age of AI
events.summary:
AI now sits on both sides of the security fight, and the vocabulary has changed with it. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled, up 56% year over year. Those breaches cost an average of $6 million, about $1 million above the $4.99 million global […]

The post 27 Cybersecurity Terms to Prepare You for the Age of AI appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
AI now sits on both sides of the security fight, and the vocabulary has changed with it. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled, up 56% year over year. Those breaches cost an average of $6 million, about $1 million above the $4.99 million global average.

Attackers now target the models themselves, the agents that act on their output, and the people who trust what AI produces. The reference lists have moved fast to keep up. OWASP published its Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 on August 4, 2026, and its first Top 10 for Agentic Applications in December 2025. MITRE ATLAS maps attacker tactics against AI systems the way ATT&CK does for IT.

The 27 terms below are grouped in 4 parts: attacks on models, agentic risks, AI-powered attacks on people, and the defenses that answer them. 

Part 1: Attacks on the model itself

These attacks target what a model reads, learns or reveals. NIST groups them into evasion, poisoning, privacy and misuse in its Adversarial Machine Learning taxonomy (NIST AI 100-2e2025), published March 2025.

1. Prompt injection

Prompt injection is input crafted to override a model’s intended instructions. It has ranked No. 1 on every edition of the OWASP LLM list, including the 2026 edition. LLMs have no hard boundary between instructions and data, so any text the model reads can try to steer it.

2. Indirect prompt injection

Indirect prompt injection hides the malicious instruction in content the model retrieves: an email, a web page, a PDF or a code comment. The user never types it. The clearest real case is EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711), a zero-click flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot rated CVSS 9.3. Aim Security showed that one crafted email could make Copilot leak organizational data; Microsoft fixed it server-side in May 2025.

3. Jailbreak

A jailbreak tricks a model into ignoring its safety training, usually through role-play, fake context or sheer volume. Anthropic’s many-shot jailbreaking research showed that stuffing a long prompt with up to 256 fake dialogues can override safety behavior. Its effectiveness grows with context window size, following a power law.

4. Data poisoning

Data poisoning plants malicious samples in training or fine-tuning data so the model learns harmful behavior. A joint study by Anthropic, the UK AI Security Institute and the Alan Turing Institute found that just 250 malicious documents could backdoor models from 600M to 13B parameters. The number needed stayed roughly constant regardless of model size.

5. Backdoor (sleeper agent)

A backdoor is hidden behavior that only activates on a secret trigger. Anthropic’s Sleeper Agents paper trained models to write secure code when the prompt said 2023 but insert exploitable code when it said 2024. Standard safety training, including adversarial training, did not remove the behavior.

6. Adversarial examples (evasion attacks)

An adversarial example is an input changed in small, often invisible ways so a model misclassifies it. Think of a tweaked image, audio clip or malware sample that slips past an AI detector. NIST treats evasion as one of the core attack classes in AI 100-2.

7. Model extraction (distillation attack)

Model extraction clones a model’s capabilities by querying it at scale and training a “student” model on the answers. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reported in February 2026 that these “distillation attacks” were rising. One campaign sent more than 100,000 prompts aimed at Gemini’s reasoning.

8. Membership inference and training data extraction

Membership inference tests whether a specific record was in a model’s training set. Training data extraction goes further and pulls memorized text out. Carlini et al. extracted hundreds of verbatim sequences from GPT-2, including personal contact details, using only query access, and found larger models more vulnerable.

9. Hidden context exposure

Hi

events.title: 共享数据飞轮！特斯拉FSD v15统一“汽车与机器人视觉”
events.summary:
特斯拉自动驾驶系统迎来一次颇具视觉冲击力的升级。

当地时间11月21日，特斯拉开始推送FSD V15.0.1，新版本不仅引入实时生成式驾驶可视化系统，还升级了底层视觉编码器，将汽车、Robotaxi与人形机器人Optimus的视觉训练进一步打通。

此次升级最引人注目的变化，据追风交易台，野村证券认为，特斯拉正尝试打通自动驾驶汽车与人形机器人的视觉系统，通过共享AI视觉技术和扩大训练数据来源，构建跨产品的数据飞轮。

根据特斯拉发布说明，新版视觉编码器使用数百万条互联网视频进行训练，并同时服务于FSD、Robotaxi和Optimus。特斯拉称，这一升级使关键人工干预率改善25倍，但目前尚未披露这一指标的基准里程和具体统计口径。

野村证券在最新研报中指出，汽车在真实道路中积累的视觉数据与模型经验，有望为机器人研发提供技术基础；而机器人训练也需要进一步引入真实物理交互数据，推动模型从视觉理解走向实际操作。

FSD V15最直观的变化，是推出了Tesla Reality View，一套全新的实时生成式驾驶可视化系统。

events.content:
特斯拉自动驾驶系统迎来一次颇具视觉冲击力的升级。

当地时间11月21日，特斯拉开始推送FSD V15.0.1，新版本不仅引入实时生成式驾驶可视化系统，还升级了底层视觉编码器，将汽车、Robotaxi与人形机器人Optimus的视觉训练进一步打通。

此次升级最引人注目的变化，据追风交易台，野村证券认为，特斯拉正尝试打通自动驾驶汽车与人形机器人的视觉系统，通过共享AI视觉技术和扩大训练数据来源，构建跨产品的数据飞轮。

根据特斯拉发布说明，新版视觉编码器使用数百万条互联网视频进行训练，并同时服务于FSD、Robotaxi和Optimus。特斯拉称，这一升级使关键人工干预率改善25倍，但目前尚未披露这一指标的基准里程和具体统计口径。

野村证券在最新研报中指出，汽车在真实道路中积累的视觉数据与模型经验，有望为机器人研发提供技术基础；而机器人训练也需要进一步引入真实物理交互数据，推动模型从视觉理解走向实际操作。

FSD V15最大亮点：实时生成式驾驶视图
FSD V15最直观的变化，是推出了Tesla Reality View，一套全新的实时生成式驾驶可视化系统。

与过去主要依赖传统车辆、道路和障碍物模型进行展示的方式不同，新系统可以从车辆上方的虚拟摄像机视角，实时生成周围道路环境的三维画面。

在科技博主Sawyer Merritt发布的首次驾驶体验视频中，Reality View展示了较高的实时场景还原能力。画面不仅能够呈现道路标线、车辆和行人，还能显示车辆的转向意图，并通过悬浮箭头提示即将采取的转弯路线。

驾驶员还可以在全屏可视化、地图和分屏模式之间切换，并通过新的Quiet Mode降低车内提示音量、调暗屏幕。导航转弯提示也会直接显示在驾驶可视化画面中。

不过，初期版本仍存在一些限制。视频中，画面偶尔出现轻微延迟，用户暂时无法自由缩放视角；在FSD自动驾驶状态下，也无法直接指定具体停车位。驾驶员需要切换至手动驾驶，才能通过新的停车位箭头选择目标车位。

除可视化系统外，V15还升级了导航路线选择、停车位置推荐、坑洼和积水识别、道路标志及小动物识别，并改进了学校区域限速和恶劣天气下的速度控制。

野村：共享视觉能力，不等于机器人拥有物理操作能力
在野村看来，FSD V15真正值得关注的，是特斯拉将汽车和机器人视觉训练体系整合的技术路线。

从学术研究角度看，特斯拉利用互联网视频训练视觉编码器的做法，与V-JEPA 2所代表的自监督视频预训练路线具有相似之处；而Reality View的生成式场景呈现，则与GR00T 2等视频世界模型、世界-动作模型（WAM）的发展方向相呼应。

这意味着，特斯拉正在尝试将汽车自动驾驶过程中积累的视觉理解能力，迁移至人形机器人领域。

但野村强调，视觉数据并不能完全替代机器人所需的物理交互数据。

野村引用的行业数据表明，扩大人类视频训练规模确实能够提升机器人泛化能力。以Dyna-2为例，将人类视频训练数据从1000小时扩大至100万小时，其14项任务的综合得分从20%提高至53%；另一家同行实验室在100万小时数据规模下，泛化能力达到55%至58%。

然而，当训练数据从100万小时进一步增加至200万小时时，单纯扩大视频规模可能遭遇瓶颈。

野村指出，主要问题在于两方面：一是普通视频缺少物体接触时的力反馈信息，无法完整反映机器人操作过程中的物理状态；二是原始视频中存在大量无效数据。以Ego4D数据集为例，野村引用的行业研究显示，75.5%的原始视频片段无法通过运动信息和可见手部等筛选条件。

这一问题在复杂、多步骤任务中尤其突出。

野村举例称，假设机器人在每一步操作中的准确率达到95%，在一个需要连续完成79个步骤的商业洗衣流程中，若各步骤成功率独立且需要全部正确，最终完整完成任务的概率仍只有约1.7%。

这意味着，即使机器人已经具备相当不错的单步识别和操作能力，面对真实商业场景中需要连续执行的复杂任务，仍然可能出现明显的可靠性问题。

野村还根据行业数据和实地调研判断，当前Optimus在运动执行过程中可能最多只能连续处理四至五项任务，距离工厂生产所要求的99.99%可靠性标准仍有差距。

野村看好物理数据与边缘算力投资机会
在野村看来，随着互联网视频逐渐成为更容易获取的通用训练资源，真正稀缺的可能转向经过筛选、能够反映真实物理交互过程的数据。

野村预计，特斯拉未来一至两年可能投入约40亿美元，用于通过通用操作接口（UMI）采集物理交互数据。

其认为，未来具备商业价值的机器人训练数据主要集中在三个方向：

经过筛选的第一人称操作视频：记录真实工作场景中的动作、物体状态和操作过程。

3D深度摄像头：提供传统二维视频难以完整呈现的空间结构信息。

六轴力/力矩传感器：记录机器人与物体接触时的力学反馈，帮助模型学习抓取、插入和操作过程中的物理约束。

除了数据，边缘计算硬件同样是野村关注的重点。

野村指出，机器人需要在有限的本地算力条件下处理复杂空间信息。其引用的GR00T 2相关研究显示，将空间网格压缩四倍后，22关节机械手的准确率会从68.6%下降至34.3%，说明过度压缩计算资源可能显著损害精细操作能力。

野村预计，Optimus V3 Beta将采用AI5芯片，目标算力达到2500万亿次操作/秒（TOPS）或更高。其预测，Optimus V3可能于2027年4月开展小批量产线测试，随后在6月及2027年下半年推进规模化出货。

在软件和算法层面，野村还强调了真实机器人强化学习和智能体代码生成工具的重要性。

根据其引用的研究，真实机器人强化学习可以将插入任务的准确率从40%—76%提升至88%—96%，同时将失败率降低一半；智能体代码生成工具则能够将抓取与放置任务的执行延迟从33分钟缩短至53秒。

因此，野村认为，未来机器人技术竞争的关键可能集中在2000 TOPS以上的车载AI芯片、定制化编译器以及智能体执行框架。

events.title: Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI
events.summary:
Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, an AI-designed CPU that runs interaction nets in hardware. Agents took it from theory to 7 nm GDS, and pre-silicon tests show 4.59x performance per watt over an in-order core.

The post Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
Architect Labs has introduced Frostbite, an AI-designed CPU with a new instruction set built around interaction nets. The company states that its AI agents designed Frostbite from interaction net theory down to final GDS. In pre-silicon tests, it reports 4.59x the performance per watt of a modern in-order CPU core. 

TL;DR

Size: 1 quad (2×2 tiles) plus 4 L3 nodes takes 0.792 mm² on 7 nm. No parameter count (it is a CPU).

Runs on: Pre-silicon only. Final GDS closes at 500 MHz on 7 nm. An FPGA-hosted playground is planned.

Performance: 4.59x perf per watt (geomean, 25 workloads) and 8.77x perf per area vs 1 in-order core.

Best: 23.12x perf per watt on conv2d.

What is Frostbite?

Frostbite is a CPU from Architect Labs that executes programs as interaction nets in hardware. Programs are written in Vine, a Rust-like language, and compiled to an IR called Ivy. The chip is a mesh of tiles, each with its own small local memory. The launch post on X states that the AI agents co-designed the ISA and chip architecture given only interaction net theory.

How do interaction nets enable parallelism?

Interaction nets were introduced by Yves Lafont at POPL 1990. A program is a graph of nodes. Computation rewrites pairs of nodes connected through their ports. Each node has 1 principal port, so active pairs never overlap and can fire in any order. Every value is used exactly once, so there is no shared mutable state to guard.

A 5-queens net has 3,183 interactions and a 262-step critical path. About 12 interactions are ready per step. Software runtimes such as HVM2 already run interaction nets on GPUs. Frostbite moves the model into the ISA itself.

How is the Frostbite hardware organized?

The chip is built from tiles grouped into 2×2 quads. Each tile has front end, engine, memory and system blocks. A runtime domain adds a frame manager, scheduler, work queue and outlet. Its ISA adds wide bundles, hardware loop counters, streams, and ops that take, peek or copy values.

Each tile runs its own queued work first. If idle, it takes work from a neighbor. If none is found, it goes inactive to save power. The company says this work stealing emerged during design and was not hand-specified.

How did AI agents design the chip?

Agents first synthesized papers and built Python models. Their output was a 141-page PDF. It was deleted after the first RTL pass because its estimates were physically unrealistic.

The research team then used ASL, an in-house, machine-checkable specification language. ASL is the single source of truth for the ISA, the Arcmodel system model, RTL and verification. The spec translates to Lean, and the project passed 800k lines of Lean.

Arcmodel first diverged from RTL by almost 250% in the worst case. An automated fitting pipeline cut that to under 6% worst case and about 1.5% median. Arcmodel simulates the full chip 660x faster than RTL. Across 4 searches and an ablation round, agents tried 58 ideas and kept 37. The design targets 7 nm, timing at 800 MHz in synthesis and 500 MHz in final GDS.

It follows Redwood, an edge AI accelerator the company announced in August 2026.

How does Frostbite perform on benchmarks?

The baseline is ‘TCPU,’ 1 core of a modern dual-issue, in-order superscalar CPU. Architect Labs does not name it, citing legal reasons. 1 Frostbite quad plus 4 L3 nodes occupies 0.792 mm². TCPU occupies 0.895 mm² on the same process.

Across 25 workloads, geomean performance per watt is 4.59x. The 10-workload search set scores 6.02x, and the 15-workload held-out set 3.83x. Results range from 23.12x on conv2d to 1.15x on fib. Performance per area averages 8.77x.

Fetch, decode and issue fall from 27% of TCPU energy to 6% in a quad. The on-chip network and scheduler take 26% instead. The fft, radixsort and LU kernels follow SPLASH-2, scaled down 64x.

events.title: 高盛谈美股“见底”三大条件：AI货币化、美联储转鸽与机构仓位下降
events.summary:
标普500指数自10月高点已累计下跌12%，高盛认为，在三个关键条件得到满足之前，市场尚难言触底。

此轮调整已超过标普500指数自1980年以来历年峰谷跌幅的中位数水平。追风交易台消息，高盛在最新发布的《美国每周市场启动》报告中指出，支持美股见底并启动反弹的三大催化剂分别为：AI投资货币化前景获得投资者信心背书、美联储政策释放鸽派信号，以及机构投资者仓位出现大幅下降。但目前来看，三个条件均尚未成熟。

尽管对冲基金已开始去杠杆，但高盛的美股情绪指标显示，整体投资者仓位仍高于历史均值。与此同时，美国股票型共同基金和ETF在过去一个月净流入约1700亿美元，资产管理机构的股指期货多头仓位处于过去十年的第82百分位。这意味着仓位层面的"清洗"远未完成，市场下行风险仍不容忽视。

调整深度超历史中位数，估值修复尚不充分
标普500指数自10月6日创下历史高点后已下跌12%，纳斯达克100指数则从高点回落20%，年内累计跌幅收窄至1%。两大指数的跌幅均已超过各自自1980年以来历年峰谷跌幅的中位数。

从估值角度看，标普500指数的远期市盈率年内已下降25%，目前降至16倍，接近30年历史均值。表面上，这一水平似乎具备一定吸引力——高盛数据显示，自1980年以来标普500指数经历22次10%以上的调整后，指数在随后3个月内平均上涨4%，其中73%的情形录得正收益。

然而，
events.content:
标普500指数自10月高点已累计下跌12%，高盛认为，在三个关键条件得到满足之前，市场尚难言触底。

此轮调整已超过标普500指数自1980年以来历年峰谷跌幅的中位数水平。追风交易台消息，高盛在最新发布的《美国每周市场启动》报告中指出，支持美股见底并启动反弹的三大催化剂分别为：AI投资货币化前景获得投资者信心背书、美联储政策释放鸽派信号，以及机构投资者仓位出现大幅下降。但目前来看，三个条件均尚未成熟。

尽管对冲基金已开始去杠杆，但高盛的美股情绪指标显示，整体投资者仓位仍高于历史均值。与此同时，美国股票型共同基金和ETF在过去一个月净流入约1700亿美元，资产管理机构的股指期货多头仓位处于过去十年的第82百分位。这意味着仓位层面的"清洗"远未完成，市场下行风险仍不容忽视。

调整深度超历史中位数，估值修复尚不充分
标普500指数自10月6日创下历史高点后已下跌12%，纳斯达克100指数则从高点回落20%，年内累计跌幅收窄至1%。两大指数的跌幅均已超过各自自1980年以来历年峰谷跌幅的中位数。

从估值角度看，标普500指数的远期市盈率年内已下降25%，目前降至16倍，接近30年历史均值。表面上，这一水平似乎具备一定吸引力——高盛数据显示，自1980年以来标普500指数经历22次10%以上的调整后，指数在随后3个月内平均上涨4%，其中73%的情形录得正收益。

然而，高盛警告称，基于趋势盈利计算的周期调整市盈率目前处于1990年以来的第83百分位，估值仍明显偏高。AI投资热潮已将标普500指数的每股盈利推升至30年趋势线以上约25%，随着资本支出顺风效应在未来几年逐步消退，盈利存在向趋势均值回归的下行风险。

高盛给出了两种情景：若投资者对盈利前景失去信心，以30年平均市盈率17倍乘以趋势EPS 340美元，标普500指数的下行目标约为5800点；若市场信心恢复、市盈率回升至10年均值，指数则有望创出8100点的历史新高。

抛售从AI蔓延至周期股，增长预期遭下调
高盛指出，此轮调整最初集中于AI相关板块，但近一周已扩散为更广泛的增长预期下调。高盛AI篮子自10月6日以来已累计下跌32%，年内跌幅扩大至4%。此前在调整期间保持韧性的非AI标普500成分股，本周也开始走弱，较高点回落约6%。

周期股相对防御股的表现同样印证了这一趋势。过去一个月，周期股与防御股基本同步运行，但过去十天周期股已落后防御股约5个百分点，显示市场开始对经济增长前景进行重新定价。

对冲基金的去杠杆行为加剧了市场抛压。高盛主经纪商数据显示，近几周对冲基金大规模减仓，净杠杆率已降至2025年4月以来的最低水平。高盛对冲基金VIP篮子（GSTHHVIP）过去六个月跑输标普500指数达14个百分点，接近该篮子过去20年相对市场表现最差的记录。

高盛将当前市场环境与2018年底的调整进行了类比。两者的共同点在于美联储持续收紧货币政策。高盛金融条件指数显示，无论是否纳入股票因素，金融条件近期均已明显收紧。

三大见底条件：AI货币化、美联储转向、仓位出清
高盛明确列出了判断市场见底的三个观察维度。

第一，AI投资货币化前景获得确认。 当前市场对AI资本支出能否转化为可持续盈利增长存在高度不确定性。一旦出现能够增强投资者对AI盈利路径信心的实质性消息，将构成重要的反弹催化剂。

第二，美联储政策出现鸽派转向。 宏观背景的改善——尤其是美联储释放降息或暂停加息信号——将有效缓解当前偏紧的金融条件，为估值修复提供支撑。

第三，投资者仓位出现大幅下降。 历史上，市场底部往往伴随着机构仓位的显著出清。然而，高盛的美股情绪指标目前读数为0.7，仍高于均值水平。美国股票型共同基金和ETF四季度以来累计净流入近1700亿美元，资产管理机构的股指期货净多头仓位处于过去十年的第82百分位。这与2018年底、2020年3月等历史底部时期仓位大幅压缩的特征明显不符。

高盛建议投资者在当前环境下，通过配置防御性板块以及持有具备强劲回购能力的公司来分散组合风险。

events.content:
11月20日，Anthropic数学家Levent Alpöge在个人网站发布说明，宣布自己与Claude共同找到了黎曼假设的证明。

他没有交出人类可读的论文，而是直接放出一个Lean 4代码库：175,187个文件、约1700万行代码。黎曼假设1859年由Bernhard Riemann提出，是克雷数学研究所悬赏100万美元的千禧年问题之一，至今已悬置约167年。

次日，Lean Focused Research Organization与Mathlib Initiative联合表示：“我们有充分信心认为，Alpöge关于黎曼假设的证明是正确的。”据《卫报》报道，两家机构是在审阅其Lean代码后作出这一表态的。MIT数学家Andrew Sutherland也独立编译了该结果，他说：“这确实是一个历史性的时刻，世界已经改变。”

然而就在同一天，另一份文稿出现了。

数学家J. L. Nielsen（署名单位为堪萨斯州Center for Topological Physics）于11月20日发布论文《Alpöge所提黎曼假设证明的无效性》。她的判断非常直接：“发布内容不包含黎曼假设的证明。所提证明无效。”

反转：几何条件是“永远为真”
Nielsen检查的是那份175,187个文件的Lean归档，逐条追踪顶层定理的证明项依赖。她认为Lean算对了，但算的东西是空的。

Lean是“证明助手”，它不判断一个数学想法高不高级，只检查一件事：从你写下的定义出发，能不能一步步推到结论。

Nielsen翻查源码后发现，证明路径中需要一类“几何对象”作为见证（witness，即用来支撑某个论断的具体例子）。但代码里这个条件是这样写的：

anyGeometry : GeoP := fun _ _ _ => True

翻译成人话就是：不管输入什么，一律返回“成立”。

第一处是几何条件。代码中有一个名为anyGeometry的谓词，定义为fun _ _ _ => True——无论输入什么，它都返回“真”。按论文的说法，这个定义在24个文件中被使用了118次，其中包括最终证明链上的关键“见证”（witness，即论证中需要举出的具体对象）。

第二处是几何对象本身。代码用一个名为geoDegenerate的“退化模型”充当几何见证：体积为0、范数为0、曲线退化成一个点、曲面类型为空集。所有正性条件（如nef、big）都被定义为True。论文写道，这个模型“只携带一个旗流形的度数数字，背后没有任何簇”。

第三处是高度函数。证明需要某个几何对象具有一个“高度”（height，可粗略理解为衡量对象复杂程度的数值），并被夹在上下界之间。但代码里，这个高度先被设为0，随后被直接改写成一个显式公式hExpl6，于是“高度=公式”这一步由rfl（自反性，即“因为定义如此”）自动成立。论文的原话是：高度“不是从任何几何对象推导出来的，而是一个公式，被选中以让论证闭合”。

Nielsen认为，几何侧与解析侧被这三步强制成了同一个对象，本该“夹住”独立几何高度的不等式，实际是“一个量和它自己比较”。

Nielsen的结论是：这些条件属于“空真（vacuously true）”——她写道：“形式化所证明的只是同义反复——黎曼假设等于黎曼假设。”即形式上为真，但没有断言任何实质内容。（The proposed proof is invalid: what has been checked is a term whose structural witnesses are vacuously true, not the argument those witnesses stand for.）。

所提出的证明是无效的：所检验的是一个结构性证据空洞成立的术语，而不是这些证据所代表的论点。

支持者：内核通过就是通过
另一边的声音同样响亮。

Lean与Mathlib社区的验证针对的是另一组问题：顶层定理是否匹配Mathlib中标准的RiemannHypothesis定义、代码能否编译、多个独立检查器是否接受。这些检查全部通过，且代码中没有axiom（额外公理）、没有sorry（占位符）、没有native_decide（绕过内核的判定）。

在他们看来，这已经足够：一个类型正确的封闭项，就是该陈述的证明。

Polymarket在11月22日发帖概括了这场争议：“新分析声称AI辅助的黎曼假设证明无效，尽管它已在Lean中成功验证。”这条帖子获得76.8万次浏览，评论区迅速分裂。

大量反驳指向Nielsen本人。有用户翻出她的PhilPapers记录，称她此前对OpenAI的Yang-Mills证明、Navier-Stokes证明都发过类似“无效”论文；也有人指出“Center for Topological Physics”的出版物列表上只有她一人。一条高赞评论写道：“Lean说有效，一位数学家说无效，你赌谁？”

也有技术性反驳。有用户称，尼尔森“犯了一个新手错误：以为恒真的前提可以平凡地推出黎曼假设”——言下之意，恒真前提只能让那一步无内容，不能自动让最终结论失效。

争议的核心：定义算不算数学
这场争论真正卡住的地方，是形式验证的两个层次被混在了一起。

第一层：在给定定义和公理下，代码是否导出了目标定理？Lean社区的回答是肯定的。

第二层：这些定义是否忠实对应了研究者想表达的数学内容？Nielsen的回答是否定的。

用大白话说：Lean能保证“从你写下的规则出发，推理没有一步走错”，但不能保证“你写下的规则就是你想说的那件事”。如果规则里埋了一句“几何条件永远成立”，那么依赖它的推理再严密，也没有真正触及几何。

有媒体的报道概括称：争议“并非单纯指控Lean编译器出错，而是针对证明中部分数学对象的定义提出异议”；同时强调，Nielsen的论文“仍属可接受公开检验与反驳的研究主张，而非数学界已取得共识的最终判决”。

人类可读版本的缺席
还有一个细节让争论难以收场：没有论文。

传统数学证明，同行可以逐行阅读、质疑、重写。而这次，外界面对的是一座1700万行的代码库。Nielsen在论文中说明，她读了约70个文件，多数是全文，聚焦顶层文件与第1至7节点名的定义和引理——相对于175,187个文件，这是一个极小的采样。

这意味着双方其实都还没有完成“人类层面的消化”。MIT数学家Andrew Sutherland在验证通过当天就说：“要理解证明的数学细节，还有很多工作要做。我迫不及待想钻研进去。”

events.title: Meta TLX Brings Warp-Group GPU Control to Triton on Hopper, Blackwell, AMD
events.summary:
Meta has detailed TLX, its Triton Low-Level Extensions that add warp-group, barrier, TMA and cluster control to Python Triton kernels. It runs Meta's ads and LLM workloads on Hopper, Blackwell and AMD MI350 GPUs.

The post Meta TLX Brings Warp-Group GPU Control to Triton on Hopper, Blackwell, AMD appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
Meta has published a detailed report on TLX (Triton Low-Level Extensions). It is the GPU compiler extension behind Meta’s production ML kernels. Meta TLX is a Triton extension that exposes warp groups, barriers, TMA and clusters to Python kernels. It targets NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell plus AMD MI300 and MI350-series GPUs. For kernel engineers, the message is CUDA-level control without leaving Triton.

TL;DR

What it is: an extension to Triton, not a new language. A Blackwell GEMM takes roughly 200 lines of Python-level Triton.

Runs on: NVIDIA Hopper (H100) and Blackwell (B200, GB200), AMD MI300 and MI350-series. MIT-licensed.

Performance: within -0.9% to +3.7% of cuBLAS on 6 H100 FP16 GEMM shapes (PyTorch).

Best: a 4x speedup on an H100 linear compression kernel for ads inference (Meta).

Worst: dense LLM-style attention forward reaches about 87% of FlashAttention-4 on B200 (PyTorch).

Bottom line: Best: hand-tuned performance from short Triton code. Worst: all numbers are self-reported, with no independent benchmarks yet.

What is TLX and what problem does it solve?

Triton programs GPUs at the block level. CUDA programs them at the thread level. Modern GPUs need something in between.

Hopper introduced warp specialization and the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA). Blackwell added tensor memory (TMEM), cluster execution and paired-CTA execution. Meta says CUDA could express these patterns, but only with large amounts of architecture-specific code.

TLX fills that gap with a model the research team calls MIMW (Multi-Instruction, Multi-Warp). The warp group becomes the basic unit of orchestration. Triton still defines what runs. TLX defines how it is orchestrated. Engineers write ordinary Triton and add TLX calls only where control matters.

How does TLX work?

TLX adds 5 extension areas on top of Triton:

Warp-group orchestration: warp groups get roles such as producer, consumer and epilogue.

Synchronization: warp groups sync through hardware mbarriers. Thread-level sync stays with the compiler.

Memory orchestration: direct access to TMA, asynchronous tensor-core ops and TMEM.

Cluster execution: multiple CTAs cooperate through distributed shared memory and cluster-wide barriers.

Optional layouts: the compiler infers layouts. Programmers override them only for speed.

The API reads like Triton. Meta’s Blackwell matmul example uses tlx.local_alloc, tlx.alloc_barriers, tlx.async_task, tlx.async_dot and tlx.barrier_wait.

How fast is TLX? Benchmarks

All figures below are self-reported by Meta:

H100 GEMM: across 6 FP16 shapes, TLX lands between -0.9% and +3.7% of cuBLAS. On 8192x8192x8192 it reaches 577.0 TFLOPS versus 582.3 for cuBLAS (PyTorch).

MI350 GEMM: TLX beats rocBLAS by 11.8% to 15.2% on square shapes from 256 to 2048.

B200 attention: On production jagged shapes, Meta’s Jagged Flash Attention beats FlashAttention-4 by about 13% forward. Backward runs about 50% faster. On dense LLM-style shapes, forward reaches about 87% of FA4 (PyTorch).

Code size: that attention kernel is about 3.2K lines. Meta estimates FA4 at 10K lines of CuTe DSL.

The research team adds that TLX trails state-of-the-art attention most on the smallest causal-forward cases. The gap narrows as sequence length grows.

 

Where is TLX used in production at Meta?

Meta’s engineering post lists 3 case studies:

Generative Ads Model (GEM) training: 20% to 25% end-to-end MFU on thousands of GPUs. TLX delivered up to 2x forward speedup for Generalized Dot Product Attention.

In-Kernel Broadcast Optimization (IKBO): a warp-specialized linear compression kernel hit 4x speedup on H100. FlashAttention under IKBO cut compute-intensive net latency by up to two-thirds.

Distributed grouped GEMM: fuses mixture-of-experts matmuls with communication for LLM pretraining on Blackwell. Meta gives no speedup figure.

Meta also compared CUTLASS, CuTe DSL and TLX on Blackwell for GEM. It says TLX gave the best productivity-performance balance
